description: Findings judged real but not fixed by the task that found them. Read by the lead at each post-task review, and promoted into tasks/prd.json when worth doing. Not part of any task's brief: no role file or doc points subagents here.

conventions.status: open | check (may already be fixed) | promoted (to the prd task named in notes) | wontfix (reason in notes)
conventions.source: the task whose review found it, or the review that did

A DVB cue that ends by its page time-out, with no clear packet, is treated as showing forever
items.notes: imagecues.go classify ignores page_time_out; a run long after such a cue opens at its start and reads the gap. Reading only.

items.title: A film whose image-track Cues cannot be parsed has them re-read and warned about on every scan
items.notes: No marker for unreadable; image_cues stays NULL and loadSeen selects it again.

items.title: A seek inside a long-showing image cue pays the cue's whole age, uncapped
items.notes: Measured 0.3 MB and 0.04 s per second of age at 640x360; a 4K film costs more and is unmeasured. A cap would drop a cue on screen, so it needs a viewer-visible decision. Promoted to JS-089 (2026-11-12).

items.title: Helper-kill replacement check allows a replacement starting after the first missing segment
items.notes: TestAKilledHelpersChunk... only requires replacement.Start >= dead.Next (no duplicates). A replacement starting several segments after the first missing one passes if another job made the gap, so the 'from the first segment missing' property is not enforced.

items.title: TestMoreWorkersFinishTheFilmSooner drops the 3-worker case on fewer than 3 cores
items.notes: On a 2-CPU runner counts is reduced to {1,2} and the 3-worker measurement is logged as not measured. This is a case dropped for core count in a test that still exists; the replacement mechanism test runs 2 and 3 workers regardless of cores, so the replacement's verdict is unaffected.

items.title: Shown speed vs recorded speed uses a 25 percent tolerance
items.notes: TestAWorkersShownSpeedIsTheOneItRecordedAndHoldsAcrossAPause compares shown speed with the recorded value using before < recorded*0.75 || before > recorded*1.25. This is a comparison of two measured speeds with a bound; it is not in timing-bounds.txt. It is probably stable on a paused job, but it is not exact and was not exercised under load.

items.title: TestSeekBackBeforeTheResumePoint keeps a 20 s bound that is under ten times a right build under load
items.notes: queue_integration_test.go (`time.Since(began) > 20*time.Second`, listed in test/timing-bounds.txt as a hang bound of 'a few seconds'). On a right build with one contended CPU (taskset -c 0 plus 4 busy loops) the seek took 4.27 s, so the bound is about 4.7x. docs/testing.md says a bound closer than ten times a right build is a bar. A slower runner can exceed it. A wait-for-event with a context dead

items.title: Flag check on the 3x job cannot fail the 'kept above 1' half, and the recorded-speed equality can race a heartbeat
items.notes: TestSessionsDoNotFlagAJobThatKeepsUp and TestSessionsFlagFollowsTheShownSpeedOfAJobThatMayKeepUp only compare the flag with the speed in the same answer. A 3x throttle is a ceiling, so on a slow runner the job is below 1 and a build that always sets IsBelowRealTime passes. The task asks for one job kept above 1. items.title: A sleep sets the pause-time speed baseline in the metrics test
items.notes: TestAWorkerReportsItsJobWhileItRuns (metrics_integration_test.go) sleeps 1 s after jobs pauses, scrapes the speed, sleeps 5 s, scrapes again and requires them equal to 1e-9. On a slow runner ffmpeg progress still in the pipe after the 1 s can change the speed between the two scrapes, which fails a right build. The comment says it is read 'by now'. Reading only.

items.title: QA runs every touched ffmpeg test under ffmpeg 6.1, not a sample
items.notes: JS-071 took four merge-queue runs: two fixture artifacts of ffmpeg 6.1 (sparse subtitle packets muxed ahead of their video) were found by CI, not by QA's 6.1 runs.

items.title: Worker's pre-store ownership check treats its own 5s timeout as an interruption, so an outage where connects hang cancels the job instead of waiting
items.notes: In upload(), the check runs under context.WithTimeout(ctx, lease/2). If Postgres is away in the form where connections hang (packets dropped, as can happen behind a Service during a switchover) rather than being refused or reset, the error is context.DeadlineExceeded. db.IsAway deliberately returns false for that, so the code takes the errInterrupted path: the job is cancelled and its ffmpeg stopp

items.title: Reap hold-off is process-local, so a reaper that missed the outage can still forget live workers
items.notes: reapHold is read from db.Of(pool).Recent(10s), which is set only when that process's own queries or connections fail. A reaper that sees no failure, for example an api replica whose idle connection survived or was replaced without an error, forgets workers whose locks died with the old primary before they take them again. Alternative: record the lock gap in the database (a lock_missing_since colum

items.title: /healthz no longer touches Postgres, so a replica with a permanently broken database stays Ready
items.notes: The probe was changed to return 204 with no database check, as the task asks. A replica whose database is permanently unreachable (bad credentials after a rotation, a wrong host) stays in service, and every request on it then waits in db.Retry with no upper bound except the client giving up. A cap on the wait, or a separate readiness signal such as 'away longer than N minutes', would be cheap.

items.title: A staged segment file is no longer removed when the final UPDATE fails for a non-outage reason
items.notes: In Worker.upload, os.Remove(name) moved after the UPDATE and only the IsAway error returns before it. A non-away error now leaves the file on disk until the job's working directory is cleaned up. Alternative: remove the file only on success or on errWaiting.

items.title: An idle api or stream replica logs nothing about an outage
items.notes: With no scanInterval set (the default), api and stream replicas run no periodic query. internal/db/outage.go logs 'Postgres is away' and 'Postgres is back' only from the tracer, which needs a failing query or connection. A replica with no viewers during a switchover never logs either line, although the criteria require each stream and api replica to say so. An operator comparing replica logs sees

items.title: Some stream and login requests answer 500 during an outage, against the docs' 'wait rather than answer an error'
items.notes: Subtitle requests (internal/api/subtitles.go:72, 246, 336, 457) call s.Items.Source without db.Retry, and DELETE Videos/ActiveEncodings calls Transcode.Stop (internal/transcode/jobs.go:243-249) without it. A request that passed requireAuth just before the outage began, or a PlaybackInfo-style call in that window, gets 500 'internal error'. Login (POST Users/AuthenticateByName, internal/api/users.g

items.title: db.IsAway treats any net.Error as Postgres being away, so job.run marks non-database network errors as cancelled, not failed
items.notes: IsAway returns true for any net.Error, including S3 or segment-store timeouts. worker.run now adds `|| db.IsAway(err)` to the cancelled branch, so a store outage that returns a net error ends the job as `cancelled`. Such jobs are never refused, and viewers restart them without limit instead of seeing the last-attempt-failed protection. The same IsAway test would also start an outage tracker and pr

items.title: Stream-role subtitle, attachment and font reads are not wrapped in Retry
items.notes: Items.Source in subtitles.go (lines 72, 246, 336, 457) and transcode.FetchSubtitle, FetchSup and StartFonts use the pool directly. Auth now waits, so a request that starts while Postgres is away waits as intended. A request that passes auth just before the outage, or one started after a brief blip, gets s.fail 500 on the first failed query. This is the same 500 the task forbids for the stream role

items.title: /healthz no longer reflects the database at all, so a replica partitioned from Postgres stays in service
items.notes: /healthz now always answers 204. A single pod that permanently loses its path to Postgres (wrong DSN host, a network policy) is never taken out of service. db.Retry keeps its requests waiting until each client gives up. Alternative: fail /healthz only once db.Of(pool).Total() for the current outage exceeds a bound well above a switchover, such as 2 minutes. That would still satisfy the 'whole outa

items.title: Process-global sync.Map keyed by pool, and a tracker that learns only from failures
items.notes: db.Of(pool) looks the tracker up in a package-level sync.Map that Open fills and nothing removes. Every caller that was handed some other pool (tests, tools) silently gets a nil tracker that never says 'away'. Holding the tracker on a small wrapper type or in Server/Jobs/Worker fields would cost a few constructor changes and would make the missing-tracker case a compile error, not a silent no-op.

items.title: Worker logs an ERROR for a Postgres switchover it survives
items.notes: Any Postgres switchover or restart ends the worker's liveness connection. The worker logs at Error level 'the worker's liveness connection ended; its jobs go on, and it claims none until it holds the lock again and its row is there' (line 285), then at Info 'holds its liveness lock again ... its jobs went on'. Operators see ERROR lines for an event the build survives. Reading only.

items.title: Unwrapped api and stream writes can still answer 500 across a switchover
items.notes: requireAuth waits for Postgres (db.Retry on userByToken), but the handlers' own writes are not wrapped: Sessions/Playing/Progress and /Stopped/Ping (sessions.go), planPlayback writes (stream.go ~248-412), Transcode.Stop in DELETE /Videos/ActiveEncodings (stream role, transcode.go:181 -> jobs.go:243-249). A cut that lands after the token check and before the write answers 500 'request failed' (ERRO

items.title: Silent failures for abandoned requests also hide real errors from operators
items.notes: fail() now returns without any log whenever r.Context().Err() != nil, for every error and not only outage errors. A player that abandons a request after 10 seconds, and a request that fails for a bug (not Postgres), now both leave no 'request failed' line. Operators lose the diagnostic for real failures on abandoned requests. Reading only.

items.title: e2e response recorder can drop bodies still in flight when a gate ends
items.notes: test/e2e/conform.mjs appends a response only after response.text() resolves, and returns silently on error. If the browser context closes before a body is read, that response is never checked, so the gate can pass without holding it to the schema.

items.title: Schema check skips error statuses that carry no JSON body
items.notes: checker.go returns nil for a non-2xx answer whose content type is not JSON, before counting it. A 4xx or 5xx text body where the schema declares a JSON type for that status is not reported, although the spec says 'no JSON body where the schema gives one'.

items.title: Client sweep excuses a non-2xx answer whenever Jellyfin gives the same status
items.notes: test/differential/run/clients.go sweep(): a listed request answered 400/404 by jellyscale passes if Jellyfin, asked the same, gives the same status. The criterion says each listed request must answer 2xx. A listed request built with a wrong fixture (id, body) that both servers reject therefore never fails. A real route that jellyscale breaks into a 404 for a client body Jellyfin also rejects stays

items.title: e2e recorder silently drops a response whose body cannot be read
items.notes: test/e2e/conform.mjs wraps `await response.text()` in try/catch and returns on any error. When a gate closes a context or the browser right after an action (play.mjs:135 `first.context.close()`, `browser.close()` at the end), responses still in flight are never recorded and never checked. A violation in such a response passes. The 'checked N responses' count cannot show the loss.

items.title: Stub GET /Items/{itemId}/ThemeMedia is not on any differential request, and echoes a malformed id as OwnerId
items.notes: internal/api/items.go themeMedia sets OwnerId from CompactID(r.PathValue("itemId")) with no validation, and test/differential/requests.yaml has no ThemeMedia request. Calling the handler directly with no path value (an empty id) makes the checker report `$.ThemeSongsResult field OwnerId: "" is not a uuid`. The same route with a malformed id such as /Items/abc/ThemeMedia gives OwnerId "abc", which

items.title: e2e recorder drops every non-JSON response, so 'no JSON body where the schema gives one' cannot fire in e2e
items.notes: The recorder returns early unless content-type matches /json/. If a route the schema types as JSON answers 200 with text/html (such as an SPA fallback) or an empty body with another content type, jellyfin-web receives it, nothing is recorded, and the gate passes. The differential tier does pass the content type, so only e2e has the hole. Reading evidence only: the filter sits at conform.mjs:14.

items.title: Sweep sends every listed request, startup included, with the signed-in token, and ignores each row's auth field
items.notes: Startup requests (/System/Info/Public, /Users/Public, /QuickConnect/Enabled) are sent by clients before sign-in with no Token. The sweep always sends the user's token and never reads the row's `auth` field, so a regression that makes those routes require auth passes. This is the criterion's 'Authorization header form' item: it is listed but never sent.

items.title: A listed request that answers non-2xx is excused when Jellyfin gives the same status
items.notes: The criterion says each listed request must answer 2xx and never 404. sweep() skips a failure when `reference.answers(r, status)` returns true, meaning Jellyfin answered the same status. A route that 404s on both servers (for example because of a fixture id mismatch) is excused, and the schema check never sees its answer.

items.title: The search-hints capture note states observations its JSON does not record
items.notes: compat/captures/search-hints-12.4.md describes limit=0, limit=-1, limit=3&startIndex=3, userId=zzz (400) and a one-letter 'a' request; compat/captures/search-hints-12.4.json holds none of them. Re-observe on Jellyfin 12.4 and record them, or drop the claims.

items.title: /Search/Hints ignores startIndex
items.notes: The note says Jellyfin takes startIndex after the limit cut (limit=3&startIndex=3 gives no hints). internal/api/search_hints.go never reads it. Fluster does not send it.

items.title: /Search/Hints reads a non-numeric limit as 0 and ignores a malformed userId
items.notes: limit, _ = strconv.Atoi(value): limit=abc answers 200 with no hints. The note says Jellyfin answers 400 for userId=zzz. Observe Jellyfin's answer for limit=abc first.

items.title: /Search/Hints with no limit or no includeItemTypes answers unobserved behaviour
items.notes: defaultHintLimit = 100 is a guess (the code says so); with no includeItemTypes seasons and collections may come back. Observe both on Jellyfin 12.4.

items.title: Hint order beyond episodes is not backed by a capture, and episode order is never compared with Jellyfin
items.notes: HintOrder puts names starting with the term first and mixes films and series by sort name; no capture covers a series sorting before a film. The three-type differential request is allowlisted element by element (names differ under JS-068), so season/number order is checked only by the integration test. Once JS-068 aligns names, drop the allowlist so order is compared.

items.title: As-you-type search sends one- and two-letter terms the trigram index cannot serve
items.notes: A trigram index needs three characters; shorter terms scan items. Measure on a library the size of the dogfood's before deciding whether it matters.

items.title: Series on an episode hint is observed but not required or checked
items.notes: Jellyfin 12.4 sends Series (the show's name) on each episode hint; a client shows it under the episode. No check holds jellyscale to it.

items.title: The lost-share guard trips on a loss of exactly the share, from float rounding
items.notes: float64(len(lost)) > MaxLostShare*float64(stored): with 0.35 and 180 stored, losing exactly 63 fails the scan. The default 0.2 showed no case up to 2000 files. Compare integers.

items.title: A scan stopped by the guard can leave a new episode shown under a hidden season and series
items.notes: Upserts run before the guard; stampParents runs only after it. Lasts until a scan passes the guard.

items.title: shown_items is SELECT i.*, frozen to items' columns when the view was made
items.notes: Postgres expands * at CREATE VIEW. A migration that adds a column to items must recreate shown_items, or readers never see it. JS-045 and every later items migration.

items.title: A listed file that never probes keeps expired items of its size forever
items.notes: case item.expired && !unread[item.size]: a corrupt file of the same size holds the removal back with no log. Bound the wait or log it.

items.title: A library rename is inferred from media store and kind
items.notes: Removing library A and adding B over the same store in one config change gives B A's id, items and watch state. An explicit former-name or id key would make it deliberate.

items.title: missingGrace set to an empty string uses the default instead of stopping the start
items.notes: newScanner parses only when cfg.MissingGrace != "".

items.title: The docs check for the rollback order accepts any sentence naming rollback, api, stream and worker
items.notes: TestRunningMdGivesTheUpgradeAndRollbackOrderForWorkersStreamAndApi passed a rollback order that left the old api with no old worker (fixed in the fix round). Pin the order, not the words.

items.title: The empty-list worker test says a tick runs, but no scan loop starts for an empty list
items.notes: TestAWorkerListingNoLibrariesChangesNothingAndSaysSoOnce: the comment and the refined criterion speak of a tick; main.go starts scanLoop only when the list is not empty. The removal assertion still guards it.

items.title: A live api replica whose beat is delayed over 3 s loses ownership of its devices
items.notes: ws_replica names only replicas that beat in the last 3 s; a GC pause or a slow commit longer than that hands devices to no one until the next frame.

items.title: The sockets WaitGroup Add can race with Wait during drain
items.notes: A socket accepted as the drain starts may Add after Wait began.

items.title: The compose stack never gives a replica its 30 s grace: docker stop kills it at 10 s
items.notes: Set stop_grace_period in compose.yaml to match shutdownGrace.

items.title: The first POST after a replica dies waits about 3 s before Caddy retries it
items.notes: lb_retry_match retries GET and HEAD only; a POST waits for the passive health check.

items.title: The readiness lead is not tied to the grace or the documented polling interval
items.notes: Nothing checks that the documented health interval is shorter than the 5 s lead.

items.title: ws_replica can stay NULL on a live device after a Postgres outage until its next keepalive
items.notes: Up to 30 s with jellyfin-web's keepalive.

items.title: scripts_test.sh checks the JS-099 record in docs/testing.md only for substrings
items.notes: 'passed 20 of 20' is matched inside the sentence saying the run was not made; the evidence lines can't fail.

items.title: The burn-in stall ('timed out waiting for playback past 22') was not reproduced or explained
items.notes: Jobs.segment waits for a job within catchUpSegments; a plausible mechanism for the stall in seeCue. Watch the failure ledger.

items.title: The JS-099 fix was verified under ffmpeg 9 only, not CI's 6.1
items.notes: The merge queue runs it under 6.1.

items.title: A Stop that matches no viewer row no longer sweeps jobs with no unstopped viewer
items.notes: Jobs.Stop cancels only jobs of the specs its UPDATE returned. An orphan job then runs until its lease or the viewer-expiry sweep ends it. Listed as a changed guarantee in the PR.

items.title: DBProxy.Delay sleeps once per read chunk, not once per round trip
items.notes: A result larger than one 32K read is delayed several times, so the schedules' 'up to 300 ms' is approximate.

items.title: A snapshot refresh that times out while Postgres is not marked away keeps the snapshot
items.notes: keepSnapshot keeps it for db.IsAway(err) || DeadlineExceeded; DOMAINS 37 says only while Postgres is away. Align code or doc, with a test.

items.title: An offline HLS segment with no mediasourceid answers 200 where the online route answers 404
items.notes: session.pick(itemID, "") takes the first film; hlsRequestFor rejects an invalid source id.

items.title: A stream replica started during an outage has no snapshot and serves no token until Postgres returns
items.notes: By design no refresh runs while Postgres is away. A replica could ask a peer for its snapshot; decide whether it matters for pod restarts during an outage.

items.title: A paused film in a background tab may drop out of the 60 s window
items.notes: jellyfin-web reports progress every 10 s (setInterval 1e4); a throttled hidden tab may report less often. A wider window (minutes) costs nothing but snapshot size, since revocation exposure is the refresh interval. Unverified that throttling reaches 60 s. Promoted to JS-103, done (#139).

items.title: Subtitle and font requests wait during an outage
items.notes: The Subtitles and Attachments routes have no Offline handler; a viewer who turns subtitles on during an outage gets none until Postgres is back. docs/running.md now says so; serving stored subtitles from the snapshot would close it. Promoted to JS-103, done (#139).

items.title: A film started in the 5 s before an outage is in no snapshot
items.notes: Stated in DOMAINS 37; the viewer waits for Postgres. A refresh after each PlaybackInfo, or a shorter interval, would narrow it. Promoted to JS-103, done (#139).

items.title: The item DTO is still a map[string]any that holds the typed sources
items.notes: internal/items/repo.go typeMedia and internal/api/items.go put media.MediaSource values into a map[string]any item. A typed BaseItemDto would carry the same guarantee to the rest of the item.

items.title: An unchecked type assertion on PlayState is left in internal/api/sessions.go
items.notes: sessions.go: info["PlayState"].(map[string]any)["PlayMethod"] = method. Outside JS-086's media scope.

items.title: The #94/#95 acceptance mutants rename a tag on the whole type, so they no longer exercise a field missing on later streams only
items.notes: With one typed MediaStream such a per-element loss cannot be built, so the mutant is harmless but no longer tests what it is named for. Rename or retire it.

items.title: keepRow's registration bound is the caller's heartbeat argument, not a table row
items.notes: context.WithTimeout(held, every) and the warning throttle use the heartbeat main.go passes; the table has no registration row.

items.title: No check that a SIGKILLed worker's job is claimed before its 10 s lease runs out
items.notes: TestAKilledWorkerIsReplacedWithinSeconds only logs the time; the before-lease claim is asserted at a 30 s lease only.

items.title: Two of the state-permission actions are never consulted by code
items.notes: actForget and actReadOwnRow are in liveState.allows but keepRow's switch decides them; drive the switch from allows() or drop them.

items.title: liveTiming looks a row up by string name and panics on a missing one
items.notes: A typo in a rare path would crash a worker at run time; typed vars computed once from the table would fail the build instead. It is also called in a 2 ms poll.

items.title: TestBeingServedFromTheSnapshotIsNotAValidation failed once in two full runs of JS-085's outage tests
items.notes: internal/api/outage_memory_integration_test.go; passed alone and in the next full run. A flake to hunt before it reaches the queue often.

items.title: An idle worker returning more than reapHold after an outage began may be forgotten by a live worker's look
items.notes: lookForTheDead forgets once time.Since(lockLost) >= reapHold, and lockLost is not reset on relock. Hypothesis from reading; a scratch test was written at ~/.cache/jellyscale/agents/js104-qa/internal/transcode/scratch_late_return_integration_test.go, not run. Run it first.

items.title: TestNoReplicaCodePathForgetsAWorker only catches reap called with a literal "" or from an exported function
items.notes: An unexported helper calling reap(ctx, pool, someVar) from a process without a lock would pass it. The removed forgot() assertion in the outage test was the behavioural guard.

items.title: The fenced put checks the clock before each put, so a slow put that began in time can finish after the lease
items.notes: Bounded by put duration, not by the 350 ms allowance; a context deadline at ownedUntil on the put would close it.

items.title: A failed start-notification LISTEN or NOTIFY is silent, so the under-1-second gap quietly becomes the 5 s refresh
items.notes: listenOnce returns on a failed connect or LISTEN without logging; sessions.go discards the pg_notify error. Behind a transaction-mode pooler notifications never arrive. Log it once, and list the session-mode connection for the stream role in ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/running.md.

items.title: No check that every stream-role route is routed to stream by the shipped Caddyfile, test/e2e/router.mjs and docs/running.md
items.notes: JS-103 moved /System/Configuration/encoding to stream and updated the Caddyfile and router but not the docs; a test comparing the stream routes with the three rules would catch the next one.

items.title: TestConcurrentStaleSyncsKeepTheNewestPosition: one of 40 concurrent UserData writes answered non-200 in CI
items.notes: internal/api/smallroutes_integration_test.go:480 'writer 26: <nil>' (status not printed). Passed 30 of 30 locally under 4 CPUs. A non-200 there is a viewer's position save failing: print the status and body, then look for a deadlock or serialization error in the UserData upsert. Log saved in ~/.cache/jellyscale/js104-evidence/.
